clinical_category: Postoperative orthopedic care - Medicare DME coordination
blueprint_topic: Resource coordination, medical-equipment orders, and payer-related discharge planning
stem: A Medicare beneficiary needs a walker for safe mobility at home after hip surgery. Which nursing action best supports appropriate durable medical equipment coordination?

options.A: Ensure the medically necessary walker is ordered for home use and coordinate with the discharge team and an appropriate Medicare-enrolled DME supplier rather than promising coverage before requirements are verified.
options.B: Tell the client that any walker purchased from any retailer is automatically covered by Medicare without a provider order or supplier requirements.
options.C: Delay arranging the walker until after discharge because DME cannot be coordinated while the client is still hospitalized.
options.D: Guarantee that Medicare will pay the entire cost because all medically useful equipment is covered at 100 percent.

rationale: A is correct. Medicare Part B covers medically necessary walkers as durable medical equipment when a provider prescribes the equipment for use in the beneficiary's home. Medicare also directs beneficiaries to use doctors and DME suppliers enrolled in Medicare and to clarify supplier participation/assignment and cost responsibility. The nurse's role is to coordinate the order and discharge resource process and help verify requirements; the nurse should not guarantee a specific coverage amount before eligibility and supplier details are confirmed. B is incorrect because a provider order and supplier requirements matter. C unnecessarily delays equipment needed for a safe discharge. D is incorrect because Medicare DME commonly involves deductible/coinsurance and other coverage details rather than universal 100-percent payment. The final item tests coordination of a real discharge resource and avoids duplicating prior questions about the functional benefit of walkers or home fall-proofing.
educational_objective: Coordinate medically necessary DME for discharge by ensuring an appropriate provider order for home use and working with eligible suppliers/payer processes without guaranteeing coverage or cost before requirements are verified.
source_organization: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS); Medicare.gov
source_document_title: Walkers; Durable Medical Equipment (DME) Coverage; Durable Medical Equipment, Prosthetic Devices, Prosthetics, Orthotics, & Supplies
source_version_date: Current Medicare.gov and CMS DME resources accessed 2026-08-18; CMS DMEPOS page updated 2026
source_locator: Medicare.gov 'Walkers' → Who's eligible: Part B covers medically necessary walkers when prescribed by a provider for use in the home; Provider requirements: doctors and DME suppliers should be enrolled in Medicare and supplier participation/assignment affects costs. Medicare.gov 'Durable medical equipment (DME) coverage' → DME definition and medically necessary/provider-ordered home-use requirements. CMS 'DMEPOS' → Medicare Part B covers medically necessary DME and most items are furnished by Medicare-enrolled DMEPOS suppliers.
source_claim_supported: Current Medicare/CMS sources directly support medically necessary provider-ordered home-use walkers, Medicare-enrolled supplier requirements, and the need to verify cost/assignment details rather than promising universal coverage.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment → Management of Care: coordinate discharge planning and resources, assess referral/equipment needs, implement provider orders, collaborate with the interdisciplinary team and promote continuity of care.
correction_summary: Total differentiation rebuild. The source item duplicated prior home-safety/adaptive-equipment content by merely stating that DME supports mobility and ADLs. The final version tests accurate Medicare DME coordination: medical necessity, provider order for home use, appropriate supplier coordination and avoidance of unsupported coverage guarantees.
audit_findings: The original item was clinically reasonable but semantically overlapped with earlier home-safety and adaptive-equipment content.
Fresh Medicare/CMS review directly supports walker coverage as medically necessary DME prescribed for home use and identifies Medicare-enrolled supplier requirements.
The final item stays within nursing scope by coordinating orders/resources and explicitly avoiding a unilateral guarantee of insurance coverage or cost.
Distractors test automatic retail coverage, post-discharge delay and 100-percent-payment guarantee; none is defensible.
